problem.statement_latex: For an unknown graph $G$ on $[n]$, a query on $S\subseteq[n]$ returns $|E(G[S])|\bmod2$. Recover the edge set. Complexity counts these parity queries rather than individual adjacency bits.
problem.statement_text: For an unknown graph $G$ on $[n]$, a query on $S\subseteq[n]$ returns $|E(G[S])|\bmod2$. Recover the edge set. Complexity counts these parity queries rather than individual adjacency bits.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(\sqrt m\log m)$ queries for sparse graphs, $O(d\log m)$ for maximum degree $d$, and $O(1)$ for the specified star/clique families, by Montanaro--Shao.
quantum.headline_text: $O(\sqrt m\log m)$ queries for sparse graphs, $O(d\log m)$ for maximum degree $d$, and $O(1)$ for the specified star/clique families, by Montanaro–Shao.

classical.headline_latex: $\Omega(m\log(n^2/m))$ binary-query information is needed over arbitrary $m$-edge graphs; bounded-degree families give $\Omega(nd\log(n/d))$. Classical parity-query reconstruction attains polynomial or logarithmically larger bounds through learning the quadratic form.
